subject: Multiple Groups with Constrained Lavaan Model

messages.author: 30a3c167fd7a21c8
messages.subject: Multiple Groups with Constrained Lavaan Model
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently running the fixed RI-CLPM model from Haymaker with constrained auto-regressive and cross lagged relations over time (shown below). I now want to test “sex” as a potential moderator.  Would this involve comparing a version of the RI-CLPM in which there are no constraints across the groups, with a modified version of the model in which the lagged regression coefficients are constrained across the groups? If so, how would I need to modify the model below to achieve this.

Thank you in advance,
Maya

RICLPM2 <- '
  # Create between components (random intercepts)
  # RIx =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3 + 1*x4 + 1*x5
  # RIy =~ 1*y1 + 1*y2 + 1*y3 + 1*y4 + 1*y5
 
  RIx =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3 + 1*x4
  RIy =~ 1*y1 + 1*y2 + 1*y3 + 1*y4
 
  # Create within-person centered variables
  wx1 =~ 1*x1
  wx2 =~ 1*x2
  wx3 =~ 1*x3
  wx4 =~ 1*x4
  # wx5 =~ 1*x5
  wy1 =~ 1*y1
  wy2 =~ 1*y2
  wy3 =~ 1*y3
  wy4 =~ 1*y4
  # wy5 =~ 1*y5
 
  # Estimate lagged effects between within-person centered variables
  wx2 ~ a*wx1 + b*wy1
  wy2 ~ c*wx1 + d*wy1
  wx3 ~ a*wx2 + b*wy2
  wy3 ~ c*wx2 + d*wy2
  wx4 ~ a*wx3 + b*wy3
  wy4 ~ c*wx3 + d*wy3
  # wx5 ~ a*wx4 + b*wy4
  # wy5 ~ c*wx4 + d*wy4
 
  # Estimate covariances between residuals of within-person centered variables
  # (i.e., innovations)
  wx2 ~~ wy2
  wx3 ~~ wy3
  wx4 ~~ wy4
  # wx5 ~~ wy5
 
  # Estimate covariance between within-person centered variables at first wave
  wx1 ~~ wy1 # Covariance
 
  # Estimate variance and covariance of random intercepts
  RIx ~~ RIx
  RIy ~~ RIy
  RIx ~~ RIy
 
  # Estimate (residual) variance of within-person centered variables
  wx1 ~~ wx1 # Variance
  wy1 ~~ wy1
  wx2 ~~ wx2 # Residual variance
  wy2 ~~ wy2
  wx3 ~~ wx3
  wy3 ~~ wy3
  wx4 ~~ wx4
  wy4 ~~ wy4
  # wx5 ~~ wx5
  # wy5 ~~ wy5
'
 ( RICLPM2.fit <- lavaan(RICLPM2,
                           data = dat2,
                           missing = 'ML',
                           group = "demo_sex_v2.1",
                           meanstructure = T,
                           int.ov.free = T
)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Groups with Constrained Lavaan Model
parts:
Maya--
     Yes, your understanding is correct. With a discrete moderator (if you treat "sex" this way), then differences in parameter values across groups imply moderation effects.
     As is general with lavaan, if there is one way to do something, there are actually several ways to do it. To allow for different effects in two groups, replace the single labels for individual parameters with two labels within a c() operator. So this line of your code:

would become

wx2 ~ c(a.m, a.f)*wx1 + c(b.m, b.f)*wy1

if you wanted to code the two sex groups as "m" and "f." Remember that, in lavaan syntax, a period (.) is just another character. Some people recommend underscore (_) for better readability.

     This coding suggests two different values for each parameter estimate. To explicitly specify equality across groups, you might end your syntax with a series of equality statements, using the == operator, as in:

a.m == a.f
b.m == b.f 

So you would have one general batch of syntax for both instances (constrained and not constrained) and then the additional lines for the model constraining parameter estimates to equality. Or you could comment out (using #) the equality constraints in the version allowing the estimates to be free across groups.
